about: What testdb.py knows. Edit this file to teach it a database package, a test runner or a way tests empty a database.
packages: npm packages that reach a database. A node app with none of them (nor a workspace of the repo it uses
that lists one), and no file that imports node:sqlite or bun:sqlite, has no database to empty, unless a test file
runners: npm packages that run tests: a package.json that lists one has tests, also without a test script.
setups: a node app's test set-up files that count without a config naming them; app_env: the .env files of its app.
resets: Python regular expressions, joined with |: a test file whose text matches one resets or empties a database.
SQL counts in capitals (TRUNCATE), and in small letters only as a statement (truncate table, delete from x where),
so a CSS class or a function named truncate, or a test named 'delete from the cart', is no reset.
drivers: two names for one kind of database server, compared as one (Laravel's own driver names on the right).
advice: per stack, how its tests get a database of their own.
words: the line per verdict; %(tests)s, %(app)s and %(advice)s are filled in.
other: files of a stack testdb.py does not read: there it cannot tell which database the tests reach.

advice.laravel: a test database of its own (in phpunit.xml <env name="DB_DATABASE" value="<name>_test" force="true"/>, plus <env name="DB_URL" value="" force="true"/> when .env sets DB_URL, as its URL names the database (DATABASE_URL: the same line with that name); and that database made once)
advice.django: a TEST NAME of its own in DATABASES
advice.node: a test database of its own in .env.test or the test set-up file (a name that ends in _test)

words.own: a database of their own: running them is safe.
words.none: no database to empty: running them is safe.
words.same: SAME DATABASE: the tests use %(tests)s, the one the app uses here, and can delete every record in it. Do not run them. Ask the user, naming it: their go, or %(advice)s first.
words.unsure: NOT SURE which database the tests reach%(app)s. Ask the user before you run them, naming it: the tests can delete every record in it. Their go, or %(advice)s first.
